service_process.text: Professional carpet cleaning begins with dry soil removal, because dry particles that are not vacuumed up become heavier and harder to remove once the carpet is wetted.
service_process.publisher: Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI), white paper "Carpet Preconditioning: Its Impact on Cleaning" (citing the IICRC S100 principles of cleaning)

service_process.text: Preconditioning means applying a detergent solution to the soiled carpet before soil removal so the soil separates from the fibres. It is applied by sprayer, an in-line unit on the extraction machine or brush agitators, and it is then agitated so the chemical spreads evenly through the pile.
service_process.publisher: Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI), white paper "Carpet Preconditioning: Its Impact on Cleaning"

service_process.text: In hot water extraction, pressurized hot water is spray-injected into the carpet pile and almost immediately vacuum-extracted, flushing out the loosened soil and excess moisture; the standard's last principles are grooming the pile as necessary and drying the carpet as quickly as is practical, which also prevents musty odours from prolonged dampness.
service_process.publisher: Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI), white paper "Carpet Preconditioning: Its Impact on Cleaning"

service_process.text: Carpet manufacturer Shaw Floors recommends professional hot water extraction (steam cleaning) every 6 to 18 months depending on traffic, and says to blot spills rather than rub them and to call a professional carpet cleaner for deep stains that spot cleaning cannot remove.
service_process.publisher: Shaw Floors, Carpet Cleaning (carpet care and maintenance)
